title: Business Risk Manager II - Contact Center
description: Overview: Manage the first line of defense risk management responsibilities of the business unit in accordance with the Enterprise Risk Framework. Oversee the proactive identification, accurate assessment and reporting of risks impacting the business unit, including loss events and Key Risk Indicators (KRI's). Ensure the appropriate escalation of identified issues and the timely completion of remediation plans. Manage the team responsible for risk and control functions in the business unit. Assist the Business Risk Officer in setting direction for the department and risk policy of the organization. Primary Responsibilities: Lead the planning, execution, and reporting of the business unit's first line of defense risk management function including ensuring the documentation of key processes and internal controls. Ensure the complete and proper identification and assessment of risks in the business unit's key processes in accordance with the Enterprise Risk Framework, internal guidance, and risk management professional standards. Drive the development, execution and reporting of the business unit's risk-based testing program. Ensure control testing is performed in accordance with M&T's First Line of Defense Guidance on Management of Risks & Internal Controls and professional standards. Oversee reporting to Business Unit Management, Scenario Management and internal risk committees. Provide direct assistance/support to the First Line Risk Officer Monitor business unit performance with respect to established key risk indicators (KRIs) and prepare comprehensive KRI reporting. Ensure the accurate and timely completion of Risk Control Self Assessments (RCSAs) and other risk management reporting. Develop a process by which emerging risks and losses are reviewed and incorporated into the RCSAs and KRIs. Identify emerging risks and risks associated with new products/ services/ markets/ channels or changes to existing products/ services/ markets/ channels and oversee the reporting of these risks to management and the Markets, Products and Services Risk Committee. Ensure the effective and efficient management and reporting of issues, including remediation plans. Develop and oversee the process for identifying and reporting risk events and losses in a timely manner. Appropriately escalate identified issues to the First Line Risk Officer and business unit management. Develop, implement and oversee the maintenance of policies for the business unit. This includes the updating of policies in response to federal, state or business unit process changes. Respond to both internal and external requests in relation to departmental policies and procedures. Provide coaching and mentoring to the staff. Review and approve test results. Build a working relationship with business unit management, Internal Audit, Corporate Operational Risk and Corporate Compliance Portfolio Managers. Exercise usual authority of a manager concerning staffing, performance appraisals, promotions, salary recommendations, performance management and terminations. Adhere to applicable compliance/operational risk controls in accordance with Company or regulatory standards and policies. Promote an environment that supports belonging and reflects the M&T Bank brand. Maintain M&T internal control standards, including timely implementation of internal and external audit points together with any issues raised by external regulators as applicable. Complete other related duties as assigned. Education and Experience Required: Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 7 years' relevant work experience, or in lieu of a degree, a combined minimum of 11 years' higher education and/or work experience, including a minimum of 7 years' relevant work experience M&T Bank is committed to fair, competitive, and market-informed pay for our employees. The pay range for this position is $107,500.00 - $179,100.00 Annual (USD). The successful candidate’s particular combination of knowledge, skills, and experience will inform their specific compensation. Location Buffalo, New York, United States of America

title: Director, Americas Employee Compliance Advisory
description:
About this role Your team Employee Compliance sits within BlackRock’s Legal & Compliance function and is responsible for the framework governing employees’ personal activities. The Americas Employee Compliance Advisory team is a key employee-facing point of contact, providing clear, practical guidance on Employee Compliance requirements and supporting the effective identification, assessment and management of employee conflicts. Your role and impact Based in Wilmington, Delaware, you will lead the delivery of Employee Compliance advisory services across the Americas and provide direction to the regional Advisory team. Your remit will include personal trading and investments, private investments, Outside Business Activities, Gifts & Entertainment and U.S. political contributions. You will ensure employees receive clear, consistent and practical advice while maintaining appropriate standards of risk management, governance and escalation. You will personally oversee complex, sensitive and higher-risk matters, provide trusted guidance to senior leaders and partner with Executive Compliance on particularly complex executive matters. Beyond day-to-day advisory responsibilities, you will help shape the broader Employee Compliance framework. You will use insights from advisory activity to identify emerging risks, strengthen policies and controls, improve the employee experience and support the continued evolution of the Employee Compliance program. Your responsibilities In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities: Lead Americas Employee Compliance Advisory and manage and develop the regional Advisory team, setting priorities, service standards and accountability across employee-facing advice. Serve as a senior trusted advisor to employees, business leaders and Legal & Compliance partners, including high-touch support for senior leaders and partnership with Executive Compliance on complex matters. Oversee complex, novel and higher-risk employee conflicts matters, ensuring practical, consistent and appropriately documented risk-based decisions, conditions, exceptions and escalations. Identify emerging risks, recurring themes and control gaps and translate advisory insights into enhancements to policies, procedures, controls, training and the global Employee Compliance framework. Build strong partnerships across Legal & Compliance and Human Resources and represent Employee Compliance in relevant governance forums and cross-functional initiatives. Monitor relevant regulatory and industry developments across the Americas and support regulatory examinations, internal audit and other assurance activity relating to Employee Compliance. Use management information, case trends and employee feedback to improve program effectiveness and scalability, champion process, data and technology enhancements, and foster collaboration, accountability, sound judgment and continuous improvement. Your experience Significant relevant experience in Compliance, Legal, Risk or a related control function within financial services, with strong subject-matter expertise in employee compliance, employee conflicts or personal conduct frameworks. Direct experience with employee personal-activity requirements such as personal trading and investments, private investments, Outside Business Activities, Gifts & Entertainment and/or political contributions, together with an understanding of the related regulatory and conflicts-of-interest considerations. Demonstrated people-leadership experience, with the ability to lead, coach and develop experienced compliance professionals and build an effective team. Experience advising on complex, sensitive or judgment-based compliance matters, with strong risk judgment and the ability to balance regulatory requirements, reputational considerations and business needs. Demonstrated ability to operate as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders and influence effectively across a global, matrixed organization. Experience developing or enhancing compliance frameworks, policies, procedures, governance or controls and working across functions to deliver sustainable program improvements. Excellent written and verbal communication and organizational skills, a collaborative and solutions-oriented approach, and a bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience; an advanced legal, compliance or other relevant professional qualification would be advantageous. 
For Wilmington, DE Only the salary range for this position is USD$153,000.00 - USD$225,000.00 . Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, and benefits including healthcare, leave benefits, and retirement benefits. BlackRock operates a pay-for-performance compensati

title: VP, Finance
description: Headquarters: United States URL: https://engine.com/ About the Role We're looking for a VP, Finance to lead Finance at Engine and serve as a strategic partner to our CEO and executive leadership team. You'll own the financial strategy and operating cadence of the company, from planning and forecasting to capital allocation, business performance, financial reporting, and long-range strategy. You'll help leadership understand what is driving the business, where we should invest, and what we need to do next. You'll also be the architect of Engine's financial story, shaping how the company is understood by its Board, investors, and partners. You'll build the Finance organization and infrastructure to support Engine through its next phase of growth. That means creating clarity where there is ambiguity, building scalable processes before they become bottlenecks, and using data, systems, and AI to make Finance increasingly leveraged. Success in this role will be measured by business impact and the results of the Finance organization. What You'll Do Strategic Financial Leadership Serve as the CEO's financial thought partner on growth strategy, investment priorities, resource allocation, and profitability. Drive capital allocation decisions across the executive team — where Engine invests people, capital, and resources, and where we make tradeoffs. Bring financial rigor to pricing, monetization, new products, markets, and partnerships. Capital Strategy & Transactions Own fundraising, debt and liquidity strategy, M&A, and other strategic transactions. Build investor relationships, lead the Board story on performance, and prepare Engine for future capital events — including the reporting, controls, and governance a public-ready company requires (SOX readiness, audit committee partnership, external guidance frameworks). Financial Planning & Business Insight Own the financial plan — quarterly forecasting, long-range modeling, scenario analysis, and the operating cadence across Engine. Develop a deep understanding of revenue, margins, customer economics, pricing, payment economics, and cash flow. Build the metrics and frameworks that make the business legible to leadership. Narrative & Communication Tell Engine's financial story to the Board, investors, lenders, and partners — turning complex numbers into a narrative leadership can act on and external audiences believe. Lead financial reporting and help the CEO communicate performance, outlook, risks, opportunities, and key decisions with clarity. Build Finance for Scale Build and lead a high-performance Finance team — attracting exceptional talent, modernizing through AI and automation, and establishing systems, processes, data infrastructure, and controls that scale without creating bureaucracy. Partner with Accounting, Treasury, Legal, and external advisors to ensure Engine has the financial foundation required to scale responsibly. What You'll Bring Experience and Background 12+ years of experience across investment banking, private equity, growth equity, corporate finance, FP&A, strategic finance, or a related field, with significant experience in high-growth technology. Investment banking or private equity background, with hands-on experience in valuation, transaction execution, and capital markets. Strongly preferred. Experience leading Finance, or a major component of Finance, at a high-growth tech, SaaS, marketplace, fintech, or similarly complex company. Financial Expertise Exceptional financial modeling skills and a strong understanding of three-statement modeling, unit economics, cash flow, and capital allocation. A track record of building financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and analytical infrastructure in environments that are scaling quickly. Experience evaluating pricing, monetization, new products, investments, headcount, and other strategic decisions. Communication and Partnership A track record of communicating complex financial stories to investors, boards, and executive teams in ways that drive decisions and build confidence. Experience partnering directly with a CEO, executive team, and Board. Leadership and Team Building Experience building and developing high-performing Finance teams. Comfort operating without a fully defined playbook and building structure where it doesn’t exist. Judgment and Execution Strong commercial instincts. You understand that Finance exists to help the business make better decisions, not simply to explain what happened last quarter. The ability to operate at both the strategic and tactical level and an usually high bar for execution and bias towards action Strong conviction and judgment. You bring a point of view vs just presenting options. Compensation Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, all roles receive equity. Depending on the role, total compensation may also include an annual bonus. Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process. Base Pay Range $300,000 - $375,000 USD The Engine Edge: Perks & Compensation We believe in rewarding great work with great benefits: Compensation: Competitive base pay tied to role and experience, with equity for all employees. Some roles are also eligible for bonuses or commissions. Benefits: Check out our full list at engine.com/culture Environments for Success: Different roles have different needs in terms of the environments that drive success which is why we have a hybrid-hub model. Whether you are in one of our amazing offices or fully remote, we'll make sure you have what you need to succeed. Perks and benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and more To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/engine-vp-finance

title: Corporate Finance, Equity - Assistant Vice President
description: About the Role iCapital is seeking a highly motivated and intellectually curious Equity Accounting and Reporting Associate to join the Corporate Finance team. This role offers a unique opportunity to become a subject matter expert in stock-based compensation accounting, equity reporting, and related tax and financial reporting matters within a rapidly growing global fintech organization. This individual will gain exposure to complex technical accounting issues, strategic transactions, and cross-functional initiatives that directly impact the Company's capital structure and growth strategy.   Responsibilities Support the monthly accounting, reporting, and quarterly/annual close activities related to the Company's global stock-based compensation programs under ASC 718. Prepare and maintain stock compensation calculations, expense forecasts, valuation support schedules, account reconciliations, and disclosure support. Analyze the accounting implications of equity transactions, including grants, exercises, vesting events, modifications, forfeitures, cancellations, RSU settlements, share issuances, and other strategic transactions. Evaluate complex equity-related transactions, including acquisitions, replacement awards, recapitalizations, liquidity events, and new equity program structures. Prepare stock-based compensation disclosures and supporting analyses for financial statements, management reporting, and regulatory filings. Assist with equity-related tax accounting analyses, including deferred tax assets, tax deductions, excess tax benefits, and stock compensation impacts on the income tax provision. Support technical accounting research, documentation, and stakeholder collaboration related to stock compensation, equity transactions, and emerging accounting guidance. Serve as a key finance contact for external auditors, preparing audit-ready documentation and responding to audit inquiries. Support the design, execution, documentation, and enhancement of SOX controls and governance processes related to stock compensation and equity reporting. Assist in preparing analyses and documentation supporting global tax, regulatory, and compliance requirements. Partner with Human Resources, Legal, Payroll, Tax, and third-party equity administrators to ensure accurate processing and reporting of equity transactions. Monitor and reconcile equity activity across source systems, capitalization records, and the general ledger. Assist with capitalization table management, share reserve analyses, and related equity reporting requirements. Identify and execute opportunities to automate processes, enhance reporting capabilities, strengthen internal controls, and support process transformation initiatives. Prepare analyses and presentations supporting management decision-making and strategic initiatives. Contribute to special projects related to equity programs, acquisitions, and organizational growth.   Qualifications Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, or a related field CPA certification is preferred 5+ years of experience in public accounting, technical accounting, audit, financial reporting, or corporate accounting Strong foundation in U.S. GAAP and financial reporting concepts Exposure to ASC 718, ASC 740, business combinations, valuation, or technical accounting matters is preferred Demonstrated ability to analyze complex transactions and communicate accounting conclusions clearly and effectively Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including financial modeling, large-data analysis, reconciliations, and reporting Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple priorities and deadlines Comfortable operating in a controlled environment with a focus on governance, process discipline, and audit readiness Highly collaborative with the ability to work cross-functionally across Finance, Tax, Legal, HR, Payroll, and external advisors   Benefits The base salary range for this role is $ 110,000 to $ 140,000. iCapital offers a compensation package which includes salary, equity for all full-time employees, and an annual performance bonus. Employees also receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes an employer matched retirement plan, generously subsidized healthcare with 100% employer paid dental, vision, telemedicine, and virtual mental health counseling, parental leave, and unlimited paid time off (PTO). We believe the best ideas and innovation happen when we are together. Employees in this role will work in the office Monday-Thursday, with the flexibility to work remotely on Friday.
